models.title: Rent inflation's recent trend predicts its level 6 months out
models.reason: Beat the baseline out of sample: error 22% lower overall (10% and 28% in the two halves).
models.baseline: Rent inflation stays where it is (random walk)
models.target: Rent of primary residence (CPI), change vs a year earlier, 6 months ahead, percent
models.method: OLS of rent inflation 6 months ahead on current rent inflation and its change over the last 6 months.
models.data: BLS CPI rent of primary residence (FRED CUSR0000SEHA)

models.title: Recent market swings predict swings over the next month
models.reason: Beat the baseline out of sample: error 15% lower overall (18% and 12% in the two halves).
models.baseline: Volatility stays at the last 21 days' level (random walk)
models.target: Realized volatility of US stocks over the next 21 trading days, annualized percent
models.method: OLS on logs: next block's volatility on the last block's and the average of the last 6 blocks (21 trading days each); 80% range from recent forecast errors.
models.data: Kenneth R. French data library, US market daily returns since 1963; check on S&P 500 daily closes (FRED)

models.title: The last 3 months of core inflation predict next month's
models.reason: Beat the baseline overall (9% lower error) but not in both halves (+20% then -5%), so it is not stable.
models.target: Core CPI change next month, percent
models.method: Average monthly change in core CPI over the last 3 months.
models.data: BLS CPI less food and energy (FRED CPILFESL)

models.title: Stocks above their 12-month average predict gains over the next year
models.reason: Did not beat the baseline: error 1% higher than share of all past months with a positive next-year real return.
models.baseline: Share of all past months with a positive next-year real return
models.target: Probability that US stocks return more than inflation over the next 12 months (dividends included)
models.method: Share of past months with a positive next-year real return, among months on the same side of the 12-month average price.
models.data: Shiller monthly S&P composite, dividends and CPI (since 1871)

models.title: An inverted yield curve predicts fewer jobs a year later
models.reason: Did not beat the baseline: error 3% higher than historical share of 12-month windows with job losses, using data known at the time.
models.baseline: Historical share of 12-month windows with job losses, using data known at the time
models.target: Probability that nonfarm payrolls are lower 12 months later
models.method: Logistic regression on the lowest 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread of the past 12 months (monthly averages).
models.data: BLS payrolls (FRED PAYEMS); Treasury yields (FRED T10Y2Y)

models.title: Building permits predict next month's housing starts
models.reason: Did not beat the baseline: error 4% higher than starts stay at this month's level (random walk).
models.baseline: Starts stay at this month's level (random walk)
models.target: Housing starts next month, thousands of units (annual rate)
models.method: OLS of next month's starts on this month's permits and starts, refit every month on data public at the time.
models.data: Census New Residential Construction (FRED HOUST, PERMIT)

models.title: Building permits predict housing starts over the next 3 months
models.reason: Did not beat the baseline: error 13% higher than the last 3-month average repeated.
models.target: Average housing starts over the next 3 months, thousands (annual rate)
models.method: OLS of the next 3-month average of starts on this month's permits and the last 3-month average of starts.
models.data: Census New Residential Construction (FRED HOUST, PERMIT)

models.title: Building permits predict building-supplier revenue (POOL, SITE, WSO)
models.reason: Did not beat the baseline: error 16% higher than last quarter's growth rate repeated (naive).
models.target: Quarterly revenue growth vs a year earlier, percent
models.method: OLS of revenue growth on lagged permit growth (4-city issued units and Census national permits), lags fixed per firm; fit 2011 onward, 2020-21 excluded.
models.data: SEC EDGAR XBRL revenue; Census building permits (FRED PERMIT); city permit feeds
